A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MorphAny3D work, and all 12 pages are readable and comparable. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement, although both refer to supplementary material. The supplied scientific content is identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative evaluations and user-preference results in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2, and qualitative application and generalization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative evaluations, user-preference results, ablations, and qualitative experiments reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same SLAT-based procedure, Morphing Cross-Attention, Temporal-Fused Self-Attention, and orientation correction. No algorithmic component or inference step changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same real and Trellis-generated assets and retain the same morphing, style-transfer, and generalization demonstrations, including Hi3DGen and Text-to-3D Trellis.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains exactly the same comparators: 3DInterp, SLATInterp, DiffMorpher, FreeMorph, DirectInterp, and MorphFlow. Comparator membership in the other supplied comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The same 50 source-target pairs, 50-frame sequences, FID/PPL/PDV/AS/UP metrics, rendering procedures, and orientation-analysis sample sizes are reported. No experimental setting or evaluation procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The attention-fusion study, attention-map visualization, orientation analysis, component ablations, and failure examples are unchanged in Figures 4–6, 8, and 11 and Table 2.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; both retain the same descriptive orientation distributions.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are identical. For example, Table 1 reports MorphAny3D FID 111.95, PPL 2.47, PDV 0.0006, AS 81.00%, and UP 86.73% in both versions.

T1.justification: The SLAT definitions and attention/fusion formulas in Equations 1–4 are identical. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free morphing, semantic plausibility, temporal smoothness, advanced applications, and generalization.

C2.justification: Explanations of attention-fusion behavior and orientation jumps are unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitation concerning artifacts on extremely fine structures and the same proposed future directions.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures and the project-page link are unchanged, including the single A6000 GPU, 30 seconds per frame, 24 GB memory, and temporal-fusion weight of 0.2.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and all 95 bibliography entries are identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv margin stamp changes, from v1 dated 1 Jan 2026 to v2 dated 14 Feb 2026. The paper's wording, headings, and organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All 11 figures, both tables, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Pages 2–12 render identically; first-page visual differences are confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The later PDF preserves the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and presentation. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its corresponding link produces no meaningful change in overall paper quality.
